issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see or feel. The danger only appears if the passenger airbag goes off in a crash.
issues.why: The passenger airbag inflator uses a propellant that breaks down with age, heat and humidity, so it can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin. Ford told owners of many of these cars not to drive until it was replaced, and later recalls covered faulty replacement inflators too.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls right away. If one is open, do not drive the car; ask the dealer to tow it or arrange the free repair.

issues.t: ABS valves stick, brake pedal travels farther
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks lower than usual before the car slows, and stopping takes more distance.
issues.why: Valves inside the ABS hydraulic unit can react with certain brake fluid additives and fail to close all the way, letting pedal travel grow. Ford recalled these cars to flush the system and test or replace the unit.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have it checked before regular driving. Check your VIN for the ABS unit recall and get the free repair.

issues.t: Driver floor mat can snag the gas pedal
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks or feels like it does not return fully, especially with an all-weather mat in place.
issues.why: The driver floor mat can slide forward and catch the accelerator. Ford supplied new mats under a recall.
issues.next: Take out any loose or stacked mats now. Check your VIN for the floor mat recall and use only a properly secured mat.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit leak or burnt fluid
issues.eng: AWD models (3.0L V6, 3.5L V6, 2.0L EcoBoost, 2.7L EcoBoost)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, drips near the front of the engine bay or under the car, and sometimes a whine.
issues.why: The power transfer unit that sends power to the rear wheels runs hot and holds little fluid. Its seals leak and the fluid breaks down, and the unit has no easy way to check or top up.
issues.next: Have the unit inspected for leaks and the fluid condition checked. Fixing seals early can keep the unit from failing.

issues.t: Throttle body fault causes limp mode
issues.sym: A wrench light or check engine light comes on and the car suddenly loses power, holds a fixed engine speed, idles roughly or stalls.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body can wear or build up deposits, and the engine computer limits power when it sees a mismatch. NHTSA investigated and Ford extended coverage on the part.
issues.next: Get the codes read. Drive gently to a shop; a cleaning or new throttle body usually fixes it. Ask a dealer whether your car falls under the extended coverage program.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a power steering warning message. It may come back after a restart and then fail again.
issues.why: The electric steering rack can fail, and on 2011-2012 cars a sensor fault in the steering motor can shut off assist. Ford recalled the 2011-2012 cars for a new gear or software.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. You can still steer with extra effort, so slow down and pull over safely. Check your VIN for the steering recall and have the system repaired before regular driving.

issues.t: Fuel tank can crack from EVAP purge valve fault
issues.sym: A gas smell, a check engine light, or a hard time filling the tank.
issues.why: A faulty vapor canister purge valve can pull excess vacuum in the tank, which may crack it and leak fuel. Ford updated software and replaced parts under a recall.
issues.next: A fuel smell is a fire risk; have it inspected right away. Check your VIN for the purge valve recall.

issues.t: Wheel studs can break on 17-inch steel wheels
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: Certain 17-inch steel wheels could let the lug studs crack, and in the worst case a wheel could come off. Ford recalled these cars to inspect and replace parts.
issues.next: Stop driving if a wheel feels loose or noisy. Check your VIN for the wheel stud recall.

issues.t: Engine overheating and fire risk
issues.sym: Overheating warning, coolant loss, white smoke or a hot oil smell, sometimes a misfire.
issues.why: Coolant leaks or a low coolant level can overheat the cylinder head until it cracks and leaks oil onto hot parts. Ford recalled these engines for software and later added a coolant level sensor.
issues.next: If the temperature warning comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the repair done before regular driving.

issues.t: Manual transmission clutch can break
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive, grinding or clunking from the clutch area, or fluid leaking under the middle of the car.
issues.why: The clutch pressure plate can fracture and damage the transmission case. Ford recalled 2013-2014 Fusions with the 1.6L EcoBoost and 6-speed manual (18V-169), and in 2026 reopened the campaign for cars whose earlier repair was not done correctly (26V-376).
issues.next: If the clutch behaves oddly, stop driving and have the car towed. Check your VIN for the clutch recall even if it was repaired before.

issues.t: Shifter cable bushing can detach (rollaway risk)
issues.sym: The shift lever does not match the gear shown, the key comes out when the car is not truly in Park, or the car creeps after you select Park.
issues.why: A bushing that links the shift cable to the transmission can break down and fall off, so the transmission may not be in the gear you chose. Ford recalled these cars more than once to fit a new bushing.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the fix is done. Check your VIN for the shifter cable recalls and get it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Door won't stay latched
issues.sym: A door-ajar light stays on with the doors shut, or a door fails to latch or swings open while driving.
issues.why: A small part inside the door latch can break, so the latch does not catch properly. Ford replaced latches in several rounds of recalls.
issues.next: Do not drive with a door that will not latch. Check your VIN for door latch recalls, including follow-up campaigns for earlier repairs.

issues.t: Steering motor bolts corrode, assist cuts out
issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets heavy, often with a warning message, mostly on cars from salt-belt states.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the bolts that hold the electric motor to the steering gear until the motor separates. Ford recalled cars in salt-use states to replace and seal the bolts.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Slow down and steer to safety with extra effort. Check your VIN for the steering bolt recalls and get the repair before regular driving.

issues.t: Fuel delivery module can crack and leak
issues.sym: A gas smell, especially after filling up, or fuel dripping under the rear seat area.
issues.why: The fuel pump module on top of the tank could crack and leak. Ford recalled it for replacement.
issues.next: Fuel leaks are a fire risk. Park outside and get it inspected now, and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Steering gear missing retaining clip
issues.sym: Loose or vague steering, a clunk when turning, or a steering warning.
issues.why: Some steering gears were built without an internal clip, so parts inside could move out of place. Ford recalled them for a new gear.
issues.next: Have the car checked before driving it much. Check your VIN for the steering gear recall.

issues.t: Airbag control module can short out
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, or there may be no warning at all.
issues.why: The protective coating on the restraint control module can crack, and humidity can then short its circuits, so airbags and belt tensioners might not work in a crash. Ford replaced the module under a recall.
issues.next: Treat an airbag light as urgent. Check your VIN for the restraint module recall.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchor cable can fail in a crash
issues.sym: No everyday symptom. The weakness only matters when the belt tensioner fires in a crash.
issues.why: Heat from the seat belt pretensioner firing can weaken the anchor cable, which may then not hold the occupant. Ford applied a protective coating under recalls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the seat belt recalls and book the free fix.

issues.t: Front brake hose can rupture
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, a brake warning light, or fluid near a front wheel.
issues.why: The front brake hoses can wear through and burst, letting brake fluid out and lengthening stopping distances. Ford recalled the cars to replace the hoses.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal feels soft or the brake light is on, stop driving and have the car towed. Check your VIN for the brake hose recall.

issues.t: Brake pedal stop pad falls off
issues.sym: Brake lights stay on all the time, or the car can be shifted out of Park without pressing the brake.
issues.why: A small rubber stop pad on the brake pedal can corrode and fall off, confusing the brake light switch. Ford recalled these cars to replace it.
issues.next: Use the parking brake when parked and have it fixed promptly. Check your VIN for the brake pedal recall.

issues.t: Steering wheel bolt can loosen
issues.sym: The steering wheel feels loose, clunks, or shifts when you turn it.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the steering wheel on may loosen over time, and in the worst case the wheel could come off. Ford fitted a longer bolt under a recall.
issues.next: Do not drive if the wheel feels loose. Check your VIN for the steering wheel bolt recall.

issues.t: Coolant leaking into the cylinders
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the car. You may see white exhaust smoke, feel a misfire or rough idle, or get an overheating warning.
issues.why: Coolant can seep from the cooling passages into the cylinders. Ford issued bulletins calling for a pressure test, computer updates, and in some cases a new short block.
issues.next: Stop topping off and driving on it. Have a dealer run a cooling system pressure test and check your VIN for open bulletins; catching it early can save the engine.

issues.t: Coolant loss and white smoke
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, white smoke from the exhaust, rough running, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: Coolant can leak internally into the cylinders on this engine. Ford bulletins describe the symptoms and in some cases call for a replacement engine block assembly.
issues.next: Do not keep driving while topping off. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and ask a dealer about the related bulletins.

issues.t: Rattle from cracked flexplate
issues.sym: A rattle or knock from between the engine and transmission, often at idle or low speed.
issues.why: The flexplate that connects the engine to the torque converter can crack. Ford issued bulletins for replacing it.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed soon so the damage does not spread to the torque converter or starter teeth.

issues.t: Torque converter can separate, loss of drive
issues.sym: The engine revs but the car stops moving, or the car won't hold in Park.
issues.why: Weld studs on the torque converter may not have been welded properly, so it can come apart. Ford replaced the converter under a recall.
issues.next: If the car loses drive, get off the road and have it towed. Check your VIN for the torque converter recall.

issues.t: Oil pan seal leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine and the oil level drops between changes.
issues.why: The sealant used on the oil pan can let oil seep out. Ford issued a bulletin for resealing the pan.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the pan resealed; a dealer can check the bulletin.

issues.t: Blown fuses stop the cooling fans
issues.sym: The engine runs hot in traffic and the air conditioning blows warm.
issues.why: Specific fuses for the radiator fans can open, leaving the fans dead. Ford issued a service message about it.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and pull over if it climbs. Have the fuses and fan circuit checked soon.

issues.t: Engine block heater can crack and short
issues.sym: Coolant leaking near the block heater or a tripped outlet when the heater is plugged in.
issues.why: The block heater can crack, leak coolant and short circuit. Ford told owners not to plug it in until it was fixed.
issues.next: Do not plug in the block heater. Check your VIN for the block heater recall.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery control module damage
issues.sym: Hybrid system warnings, loss of power, or a car that will not charge or start.
issues.why: The battery energy control module can be damaged by excess voltage and current, which can cause power loss and a fire risk. Ford told owners not to charge until the recall repair was done.
issues.next: Stop charging the car and check your VIN for the recall right away.

issues.t: Hybrid transmission thumping or grinding
issues.sym: Thumping, rubbing or grinding noises from the transmission area, often at low speed.
issues.why: The hybrid transmission can develop internal noise, and contamination inside the unit is a known cause. Ford issued a bulletin and service message about repairing it.
issues.next: Have a dealer diagnose the noise and check the bulletin before it gets worse.

issues.t: Backup camera blank or distorted
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is blank, flickers, looks distorted, or stays on the screen after you leave Reverse.
issues.why: A faulty camera on 2016 cars and a software error on 2019-2020 cars can spoil the image. Ford recalled both groups.
issues.next: Look over your shoulder when backing up until it is fixed. Check your VIN for the camera recalls.
